1.title: Pack the Bag!
1.topic: packing a bag for a trip to Gran's house while the family cat keeps jumping into the bag (family, travel, humor)
sounds: pack, bag, cap, map, cat, van
입을 옆으로 크게 벌리고 '애': bag '배그', cat '캣'. '백', '켓'처럼 좁게 말하지 않아요.
입을 동그랗게 크게 벌리고 짧게 '아': top '탑', hop '합'.
입에 힘을 빼고 짧게 '이': zip '집', big '빅'. '지-입'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
1.expression: Start excited on “We go to Gran's today.”, say each “Put in a …” line like a busy helper, sound surprised on “Look! The cat is in the bag!”, make “No, cat, no!” firm but funny, say “Zip, zip, zip!” quick and snappy, and shout “Gran, here we come!” happily.

2.title: Catch That Hat!
2.topic: on a windy walk the wind blows Grandpa's hat down a hill, a boy chases it and a little dog catches it and brings it back (family, weather, animals, humor)
sounds: k, s, p, f 소리 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t: walked '웍트', jumped '점프트'. '워크드'처럼 '드'를 붙이지 않아요.
b, l, g 같은 울리는 소리 뒤는 약한 d: rolled '롤드', wagged '왜그드'.
2.expression: Begin calm and cheerful on the walk, make “Whoosh!” big and windy, read the chase fast and breathless, shout “Stop, hat! Stop!” like Jake, sound amazed when the little dog catches the hat, let Grandpa laugh warmly, make his joke “Do you want a hat, too?” go up playfully, and end softly and sweetly.
practice: caught the hat in its mouth

3.title: Ants Work as a Team
3.topic: how ants live in colonies with a queen and worker ants, follow scent trails, lift heavy loads and work together (animals, insects, science, teamwork)
lines: *One* *colony* can have *thousands* of *ants*, | and *every* *ant* has a *job*. ↘
The *queen* *ant* is the *biggest*. | Her *main* *job* | is to *lay* *eggs*. ↘
When a *piece* of *food* is *too* *heavy* for *one* *ant*, | *other* *ants* *come* to *help*. ↘
sounds: colonies는 첫 음절 'COL'에 힘 (칼러니즈), outside와 without은 뒤 음절 'SIDE', 'OUT'에 힘! 나머지는 작고 짧게.
qu는 'ㅋ+우' 소리: queen '크윈'. '퀸'보다 입술을 동그랗게 모았다가 '윈'으로 열어요.
heavy의 ea는 짧은 '에' (헤비), weight의 eigh는 '에이' (웨잇). gh는 소리가 나지 않아요.
3.expression: Read like a friendly nature guide: sound amazed on “huge groups called colonies”, say the queen's job clearly, list the workers' jobs with a short pause at each comma, ask “But how do ants find their way home?” as a curious question that falls at the end, make “many times its own weight!” sound surprising, slow down for “Ants talk without words.”, and end with a proud, cheerful last line.

4.title: Hana's Big Idea
4.topic: a nervous girl runs in her class council election, listens to classmates at recess, proposes a Buddy Bench for lonely kids, gives her speech and wins (school, community, leadership, courage)
lines: She *wanted* to *run*, | but *giving* a *speech* in *front* of *everyone* | *felt* *scarier* than a *roller* *coaster*.
So the *next* *day* at *recess*, | Hana *carried* a *notebook* | and *listened*. ↘
*Anyone* who *needed* a *friend* | could *sit* on the *bench*, | and *someone* would *come* and *invite* them to *play*.
On *election* *day*, | Hana's *hands* were *shaking* | as she *walked* to the *front* of the *room*. ↘
She *took* a *deep* *breath* | and *shared* *what* she had *heard* | from her *classmates*. ↘
When she *finished*, | the *room* was *quiet* for a *moment*. | *Then* *everyone* *clapped*! ↘
vocab: 친구 벤치 (같이 놀 친구를 찾는 의자)
sounds: election은 'LEC', advice는 'VICE', invite는 'VITE'에 힘! notebook은 앞 'NOTE'에 힘을 줘요. 나머지는 작고 약하게.
front of, felt a, took a, heard from
자음+모음은 이어서 한 단어처럼: front of '프런터브', took a '투커'.
혀끝을 이 사이로 살짝 내밀어요. that·then은 울리는 소리, thing·three·breath는 바람만 나는 소리 ('쓰'·'드'가 아니에요).
4.expression: Tell it like a story about courage: sound nervous and quick on Hana's pounding heart, make the roller-coaster comparison a little dramatic, give Min a calm, kind big-brother voice, read the recess lines like you are listening carefully, slow down and sound gentle on “felt lonely”, say “a Buddy Bench!” with a bright smile, make the speech lines shaky and then brave, pause on “quiet for a moment” before “Then everyone clapped!”, and finish with a wise, confident last line.
practice: Just ask people what they need.
